title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning for queueing fairness, starvation prevention, and timeouts
author: Jordan Reyes
description:
Context: Production traffic patterns exposed cases where long-running KV-heavy requests could starve short low-latency requests in the continuous batcher. This caused intermittent P95/P99 latency spikes and a small but measurable increase in tail-cost because batch windows grew to accommodate slow requests. This PR tunes the scheduler and introduces several protections to improve queueing fairness and starvation prevention while preserving throughput.

Summary of changes: - Add per-priority aging so requests waiting longer are promoted to higher scheduling priority (fairness). - Separate internal 'short' and 'long' queue bins and enforce a max-queue-depth-to-batch policy to avoid unbounded waiting of short requests behind long KV-heavy batches. - Introduce adaptive per-queue timeout thresholds: short requests use a lower max-wait; long requests can wait longer but are drained periodically to prevent indefinite starvation. - Add preemptive flush for queued short requests when a batch would otherwise be filled by older long requests. - Expose two new config knobs (continuous_batcher.priority_aging_ms and continuous_batcher.short_queue_timeout_ms) and document defaults that worked in staging. - Instrument new metrics: batch_queue_length_by_bin, batch_promotions_count, batch_preempt_flushes, batch_wait_time_histogram; add traces for promotion and preemptive-flush events. - Add unit and integration tests that simulate mixed short/long request workloads and verify latency fairness and no starvation for 60s runs. - Update comments and developer docs describing the tradeoffs and how to tune knobs.

Why: Previous algorithm prioritized batch fullness which maximized throughput but could hide large latency regressions for short requests. The changes aim for predictable latency SLOs for latency-sensitive requests while retaining most throughput benefits for long requests.

Checklist: - [x] Implement aging and queue bins - [x] Add config flags and defaults - [x] Add metrics and tracing - [x] Add unit + integration tests - [x] Run perf canary across GPU pools - [x] Update docs and release notes

Commits summary: - 1) introduce queue-bin types and routing logic (batch_queue.go) - 2) implement priority aging and promotion timer (scheduler_prio_aging.go) - 3) implement preemptive flush and adaptive timeouts (batch_flush.go) - 4) metrics + tracing + config plumbing (metrics.go, tracing.go, config.yaml) - 5) tests and docs (batcher_tests.go, perf_integration_test.sh, docs/continuous-batcher.md)

Files changed (high-level): - runtime/continuous_batcher/batch_queue.go (new) - runtime/continuous_batcher/scheduler_prio_aging.go (new) - runtime/continuous_batcher/batch_flush.go (modifications) - runtime/continuous_batcher/config.go (config knobs) - runtime/continuous_batcher/metrics.go (metrics) - runtime/continuous_batcher/batcher_tests.go (tests) - docs/continuous-batcher.md (docs)

Review & CI: - CI: build: pass, unit-tests: pass, integration-tests: flaky on first run (timeout in perf_integration_test), re-run fixed it. e2e perf canary: passed in staging with 5% throughput loss and 30-45% P99 latency improvement for short requests. - Rationale vs alternatives: We considered strict quota-based isolation (dedicated sub-pools) but that increases complexity and reduces throughput for long requests; opted for adaptive/promote approach to maintain a single pool and simpler operational surface. - Backwards compatibility: All config knobs have defaults matching previous behavior unless explicitly enabled; this is not a breaking change.

Release notes: Improved continuous-batcher scheduler fairness and added config knobs to tune priority aging and short-request timeouts. See docs/continuous-batcher.md for details.

Related Linear: ENG-4321, ENG-4390.
